note: Every approved look reference of Brix Town, in one list (ADR-0061). Files live in Art/Reference/<Category>/ and are named <Category><Subject>[_<Variant>].<ext> in PascalCase, so a name says what it is. 'locks' is what the reference decides; 'decision' the ADR and the owner's approval; 'made_by' the script that renders it; 'models' what the game is built from or measured against with it; 'status' proposed when it waits for the owner's approval; 'issues' what is seen wrong in it and not mended, for the owner to judge; 'was' the old names. 'places' says which reference each kind of place in the game is judged against, and which places have none: python Tools/reference_catalog.py --for <tour stop, lot id or place> answers it; a place's 'camera' names the tour stops that look through its reference's own camera (Tools/unreal/look_match.py compares those square by square). 'gaps' are references a category still lacks. Tools/reference_catalog.py checks this file against the folders and writes Art/Reference/index.html; run it after any change here. 'unreal' (ADR-0075, docs/process/UNREAL_REFERENCES.md) is a place's light settings as pictures taken in the game: 'where' the tour stop's place, 'blender' the one Blender picture the page keeps showing, 'settings' the hour of the game each setting is shot at (hh:mm or ref, |<weather> after it), 'missing' the settings the game cannot show and why, 'issues' what is seen wrong in the game's pictures; 'files', 'checks', 'shot' and 'status' are written by Tools/unreal/reference_shots.py, and only the owner's words make its status approved (then with a 'decision' quoting them).

references.locks: The look of the world (the old-town alley of style test 02: matte mottled plaster and stone, soft rounded forms, W1-W8) at morning, midday and dusk; at night with the lamps on, and with them off under a full and a new moon; and by day in cloud, rain, fog and snow. The game's walls are large rough blocks with heavy dark joints and jutting window surrounds; the reference's are smooth dressed stone with fine joints (G3).

The buildings are not like the reference's (the owner, 2026-11-28: "some of the structures in the game are not like the ones in the blender. notice the color of wall, windows etc in blender are so much good"). The reference's café has a rough stone ground floor with three large arched windows glowing warm, upper windows evenly spaced with stone surrounds, sills and pairs of louvred shutters, window boxes, an iron balcony, a hanging sign and lit lanterns on posts. The game's has square dark shop windows with nothing seen inside by day, heavier dark window frames, no window boxes, and one lamp post far down the street.

The colours are poorer than the reference's (the owner: "review the colors used in these building in the game, the blender has better colors ... the palette and color selection both"). The palette's numbers are the same on both sides (World/rules/building_styles.json and Tools/blender/building_kit_07.py), but (1) selection: this house is warm plaster with ochre shutters and wood frames, tan on tan on brown, and the house opposite bare brown stone, where the reference leads with cool grey plaster and mixes blue, teal and red shutters; (2) the light turns it orange: sunlit plaster measures 191,162,126 here against the reference's neutral 179,175,174, paving 209,197,184 against 191,187,188, and the sky is near white (212,215,218) against the reference's blue (150,165,184), so no cool colour sets off the warm ones; (3) the plaster is a flat fill at this distance and the stone one brown with heavy dark joints (G3, G4).
A grey tower block stands over the roofs at the end of the street; the reference's street ends in a wall and a tree.

The paving is small warm brick setts with no kerb where the reference has large grey slabs and a raised kerb.

references.title: The kinds of light and their named colours, in a home's room at night
references.locks: The named colours of light of World/rules/lights.json and the fittings that share them (the owner, 2026-11-26: "when the room is lit by lights then the color should be decided by the light types"; "each colored light should have a name for different styles of lamps, lights, street lights etc. can share the color behavior"). Ten colours: Lantern amber (the palette's Lantern, for street lamps and lanterns to share), Warm white, Soft white, Neutral white, Cool white, Fire red, Neon blue, Neon green, Neon red, Neon amber (the owner: "we also need some cooler and even neon blue and green lights"; "add those 3 suggestions"). Thirteen fittings, each lit alone in the approved home room (IndoorHomeRoom) on a night with no moon and the fire out: floor lamp, table lamp, wall light and pendant in Warm white, desk lamp in Soft white, ceiling light in Neutral white, cool ceiling light in Cool white, wall lantern in Lantern amber, candles in Fire red (every fire one red, candles too: the owner, "Fire red"). Neon is an accent (the owner: "Weaker neon"): a tube of 8 to 10 W, shown with the room's own floor lamp, table lamp and fire lit, so the room keeps its colours and the tube tints its corner. A fitting's strength is its own; its colour is its named colour's. The sheet shows each fitting twice: at one exposure for all (the lamp-lit night's), and with the eye set for that light, at most 2.5 stops either way; each fitting has its own entry under Ornaments (OrnamentsLight<Fitting>), with the second picture.

The look is the court's (ADR-0069) taken warmer: honed stone drums with a line of light round each floor and timber fins round the upper drum, polished stone floor with warm caramel and dark bands and brass rings let into it, the lattice in gold, timber and cream stalls under striped canopies, timber and brass seating; uplit piers, warm kitchens, opal pendants over the long tables. In the world's light: by day the sky and sun through the egg, the lanterns low; at dusk and night the egg dark and the lamps at full. No moonlit nights, no weather. The outlets' signs are coloured glass with backlit names (ADR-0071), not raked, as they follow the drum.

references.title: Eastgate Mall's moving stairs close by, at every hour
references.locks: Every moving stair in Eastgate Mall, shown at the foot of the pair in the Great Court's middle. Their shapes are the game's: the plan's ramps (World/city_01/blocks/b_16_5.json, b_16_5_l0: from a to b, 4.4 m wide, floor to floor, 6 m over 29 m), with the game's parapet down the middle (BrixMall.cpp, 0.3 m wide) making two lanes of about 1.8 m. Close by, in the court's look (MallsEastgateCourt, ADR-0069): at each end a fixed floor plate of darker steel with a thin brass edge and a dark comb where the steps slide under it; two flat steps, then steps of 0.2 m up the slope; dark grey treads and risers, ribbed along the way they travel, mostly not metal so the sun through the roof lights shows on them, a thin brass line on each step's nose; polished steel skirts with a line of light along their top; a cream deck; glass sides ending in round newels with a brass handrail along their top and round each newel; the middle parapet the same, a steel skirt and line of light to each lane, a cream deck and a glass side with its handrail to each lane; the outside clad in the galleries' timber slats, a cream edge and a line of light along its foot; the underside in the same slats. In the world's light: at Midday the sun through the middle roof light falls on the upper part of the stairs; in the Morning and at Dusk it is too low to reach them; at dusk and at night the lines of light and the hall's lanterns at full. No moonlit nights, no weather.
